title:
VOLUME AND SURFACE AREA,
(VOLUME OF PYRAMIDS, CONES AND SPHERES)
objective: LO: I can calculate the volume of pyramids, cones and spheres using standard formulae.

key_terms.title: Volume of pyramids, cones and spheres

content.text: A pyramid has a polygon base and triangular faces meeting at an apex. A cone is a circular pyramid. Their volumes are one-third of the corresponding prism or cylinder.
Key formulae: Pyramid: V = &frac{1}{3} × base area × height. Cone: V = &frac{1}{3}πr²h. Sphere: V = &frac{4}{3}πr³.

examples.desc: one-third of the prism with same base
that is surface area, not volume

key_idea.title: Key idea
key_idea.text: Pyramids and cones have volume equal to one-third of the corresponding prism or cylinder. A sphere uses its own formula with r cubed.
key_idea.caption: The &frac{1}{3} factor applies to all pyramids and cones

modelled_examples.label: Example 1 – square-based pyramid
modelled_examples.question: Find the volume of a pyramid with a square base of side 6 cm and height 10 cm.
modelled_examples.explanation: Find the base area first, then multiply by one-third of the height.

modelled_examples.label: Example 2 – cone
modelled_examples.question: Find the volume of a cone with radius 5 cm and height 12 cm. Round to 1 d.p.
modelled_examples.explanation: Substitute into the cone formula and evaluate.

modelled_examples.label: Example 3 – sphere
modelled_examples.question: Find the volume of a sphere with radius 3 cm. Round to 1 d.p.
modelled_examples.explanation: Cube the radius, then multiply by &frac{4}{3}π.

modelled_examples.label: Example 4 – hemisphere
modelled_examples.question: Find the volume of a hemisphere with radius 6 cm. Round to 1 d.p.
modelled_examples.explanation: Find the full sphere volume, then halve it.
